user_summary:
What changed in brief 2: Fire-3d now opens on a map of California with every current fire and this year's large fires (2025 fires are one filter away). You do not have to click a fire to see it: zooming in on a fire whose analysis is ready shows how it spread, and zooming out goes back to the California map. A fire that is not ready has a card with a 'Prepare analysis (1-3 min)' button, the only thing that starts the downloads. The search box now takes street addresses, towns, ZIP codes, coordinates and fire names, and a location card answers four questions in plain words: what is near here, what officials say, what could bring fire here (the model as a dated sentence such as '0 of 31 simulated fires reached here by ...'), and how fresh and reliable that is. An 'Official now' block shows evacuation orders (Cal OES), CAL FIRE's own record and its changes, and National Weather Service fire-weather alerts, each with who issued it and when, and never mixed with the model. Public opens on aerial photos (dated June 2024 or earlier, so before recent fires), Command on a dark map with more technical detail; 3D shows simple building shapes with a 'not a damage assessment' caveat, and a satellite chip shows the newest satellite image (never live).

What I verified, with live data: one fire prepared from its card (Cyrus, 2 min 39 s), its spread then showed on zoom; a forecast run from the app; the live loop's 15-minute cycles; search, cards, official information, all views on desktop and phone, outages of every outside service, readable text (contrast 6.3:1 or better), the map's share of the screen (75.7-77.5 %), speed, keyboard use, data contracts and a secret scan (0 files contain the FIRMS key). I fixed 8 problems (listed in the report) and brought the README and docs/validation.md up to date.

Remaining issues, most important first: (1) the forecast model itself is only moderately skilful and over-predicts small fires that crews stop early (it has no firefighting in it); (2) no live Red Flag Warning existed in California during the test, so live NWS alerts were checked only with recorded samples and Eaton's archived warning; (3) the 3D Forensic view's default (high quality with depth of field) runs at about 50 frames per second on a Retina screen (about 37 uncapped in the realistic style), so motion is a little less smooth there; medium or low quality hold 60; (4) searching a town that lies inside a prepared fire's area (for example Malibu and the Bryson Fire) shows that fire's spread because you are zoomed in there, by design; (5) smaller items: the 75 % open-map target is met with a thin margin, if Fire-3d's own server is down 'Official now' keeps saying 'Checking...', CAL FIRE history only starts on Oct 18, 2026, and the past-alert archive search samples 5 points.
